flags_note: 0x01 is a drive-ready gate, NOT media-gated (command answers with no disc, proven on hardware)
dispatch: cdb[4] (subfn) selects the reply. 03 (VID) builds the format-0x80 READ DISC STRUCTURE request, gates the AGID state, and calls the OEM dispatcher; 09 (DumpAll) reads a 64-byte RAM window at the address packed in cdb[5..9]. Every other subfn writes its 16-byte payload slot: buffer cleared, written via 0xa2074, committed via 0x98180. A non-matching mode/knock tail-calls the untouched OEM handler.

subfns.02: Speed — state = ramp-ceiling cap (00 = OEM, FF = max)
subfns.04: BusEncryption — no-op (read path has no cipher; proven)

de_note: downgrade-enable: write 0xDE unconditionally so every freemkv image flashes over any prior version; not covered by the CMAC integrity regions
hardware_proven: LG BU40N 1.00, /dev/sg0: 3C 0E C0 DE 01 -> 'freemkv <version>'; 09 DumpAll reads live SRAM; DE gates downgrade (controlled test). 03 VID variant sweep awaits a disc-in test.
note: cleanroom manifest — freemkv-authored bytes + integrity hashes only, no OEM code. The Rust KAT (mt1959_kat_tests.rs) is the enforced, byte-exact source of truth; this file is descriptive and intentionally omits drift-prone goldens (output hash / CMAC deltas) so it cannot go stale against the enforced test.
